etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English rof, from Old English hrōf (“roof, ceiling; top, summit; heaven, sky”), from Proto-Germanic *hrōfą (“roof”).

definitions.definition: (architecture) The external covering at the top of a building.

quote.citation: 1913, Joseph C[rosby] Lincoln, chapter I, in Mr. Pratt’s Patients, New York, N.Y., London: D[aniel] Appleton and Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: 'Twas the house I'd seen the roof of from the beach.

quote.citation: 1931, Robert L. May, Rudolph, The Red-Nosed Reindeer, Montgomery Ward, draft:
quote.text: The very first sound that you’ll hear on the roof(Provided there’s fog) will be Rudolph’s small hoof.

quote.citation: 1984, Rock Master Scott & the Dynamic Three (lyrics and music), “The Roof Is on Fire”:
quote.text: The roof, the roof, the roof is on fire!We don't need no water: Let the motherfucker burn!Burn, motherfucker, burn!

definitions.definition: The top external level of a building.

quote.citation: 1962, Gerry Goffin et al. (lyrics and music), “Up on the Roof”:
quote.text: When this old world starts getting me downAnd people are just too much for me to face,I climb way up to the top of the stairsAnd all my cares just drift right into spaceOn the roof, it's peaceful as can beAnd there, the world below can't bother me...

definitions.definition: The upper part of a cavity.

quote.citation: 2011 October 1, John Sinnott, “Aston Villa 2-0 Wigan”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: As Bent pulled away to the far post, Agbonlahor opted to go it alone, motoring past Gary Caldwell before unleashing a shot into the roof of the net.

definitions.definition: (mining) The surface or bed of rock immediately overlying a bed of coal or a flat vein.

quote.citation: 1857, Thomas Hughes, Tom Brown's School Days:
quote.text: Tom thought his cap a very knowing affair, but confessed that he had a hat in his hat-box; which was accordingly at once extracted from the hind-boot, and Tom equipped in his go-to-meeting roof, as his new friend called it.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English rofen, roven (“to roof”), from the noun (see above).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cover or furnish with a roof.

quote.citation: 1911, James George Frazer, The Golden Bough, volume 11, page 264:
quote.text: A trench about ten feet deep was dug in the ground and roofed over with sticks and earth so as to form a dark tunnel.

definitions.definition: To traverse buildings by walking or climbing across their roofs.
(transitive, slang) To put into prison, to bird.

quote.citation: 1998 March 4, “Law and Disorder”, in Beverly Hills, 90210, season 08, episode 22:
quote.text: Did you see them, David? I mean, did you see them looking at me? I-I'm walking out of the court, and everybody was practically – yeah, they were gawking.  […]  I mean, Noah roofed me, I proved it, end of story.

quote.citation: 2000 January 1, “Stupid”, in Mr. Metaphor (lyrics), The Will Tell Compilation Vol. 1: Thats Right Inc., performed by Word A' Mouth, Block McCloud, and Mr. Metaphor:
quote.text: I’m open, hype off the chronic I was smoking, feeling zootedThat Brooklyn shit got me stupidI’m loose, kid – that’s what the overproof didWhat the ruck you looking at, son? You’ll get roofed, kid!

quote.citation: 2012 November 15, “Brown Bag Wrap”, in Rare Chandeliers, performed by Action Bronson:
quote.text: Inhale the mystical, the blue shitSee me on the stoop shit, act stupid at the park, the ball, get roofedBaby see the cops, the drugs, she boofed itFoie gras at every meal, that means I triple-goosed it

quote.citation: 2018 May 5, “Attempted 1.0”, AM (lyrics), performed by Skengdo & AM of 410:
quote.text: You don’t want war, you’re shook of itHella man dash when their friend got roofed

definitions.definition: (transitive) To shelter as if under a roof.

quote.citation: 1865, Thomas Greenbury, Pleasant Rambles Over Moors, Mountains, Mines, and Waterfalls‎[2]:
quote.text: They reached him: the pieces of rock had roofed him over—he was without injury or scratch.
It built him softly round, it roofed him warmly over, it rested, all so firm, on selection.
